children: Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust's distribution-per-unit outlook remains under pressure, say Jefferies analysts in a note. The real-estate investment trust's distribution per unit for 1H was in line with consensus and Jefferies' estimates, but its overseas net property income declined more than the analysts expected. The rate of renewed rents also remain weak in its China portfolio and at a Hong Kong asset, they note. Still, better-than-expected operating performance could cushion its future results, they say. Committed occupancy in 2Q rose 120 basis points on quarter, with broad-based improvements across the REIT's portfolio, they add. Jefferies retains its hold rating and 1.15 Singapore dollar target price. Units rise 1.8% to S$1.15. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
